title: Foundation or Formula? (full text, v1): Table 3 and Sections 4.1, 5.1
note: TimesFM-3 has the lowest mean MASE in 16 of 36 scenarios, classical methods in 20 (AutoARIMA 10). title: Foundation or Formula? (full text, v1): Section 4.4 seasonal data
note: On the seasonal ARIMA process (D4) AutoARIMA's mean MASE is 21.8%, 21.1% and 23.7% below TimesFM-3's at n = 48, 96 and 200; the ETS process shows 4 to 12%. Seasonal naive also beats TimesFM-3 on D4 at every length. With only two cycles (n=24) the order reverses: TimesFM-3 1.321 against AutoARIMA 2.284, 42% lower. Classical methods are told the period; TimesFM-3 is not.

title: [2610.00589] Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
note: Abstract, v1 of 30 Sep 2026, stat.ME. Exploratory comparison of TimesFM-3 with classical methods on 7,200 series simulated from nine known processes, 12-step horizon, protocol called pre-registered. Neither family dominates: TimesFM-3 never above 1.31 times a scenario's best, every classical method at least 2.2 somewhere; auto ARIMA 21-24% better on seasonal ARIMA data with four or more cycles.

title: Foundation or Formula? (full text, v1): design
note: Three authors, Alexandria University. Nine processes x four lengths (24 to 200 points) x 200 replications, 36 scenarios; period 12; horizon 12; primary measure MASE. TimesFM-3 run zero-shot and univariate at defaults (timesfm 3.0.1, weights revision 43046b8) against seasonal naive, Theta, AutoETS, AutoARIMA (statsforecast 2.1.1) and their mean. Not hourly, not load, no covariates.

title: Foundation or Formula? (full text, v1): post-hoc checks (5.2, 5.5, 5.6)
note: Post hoc. Month-of-year sine and cosine given to TimesFM-3 as past-and-future covariates raised its MASE in 7 of 8 seasonal scenarios (1.124 to 1.194 on D4, n=96). Randomised parameters: worst ratio 1.49 to 1.56. 48-step horizon, steps 25-48: AutoARIMA has the smaller worst ratio (1.41 against 1.80); on a flat logistic plateau TimesFM-3 forecasts a fall (MASE 8.37, seasonal naive 1.11).

title: Foundation or Formula? (full text, v1): real data, cost, licence, limits
note: 101 FRED-MD monthly series, Jan 2025 to Jun 2026, 18 steps: AutoARIMA mean MASE 0.540, TimesFM-3 0.607, not separated statistically. M4 monthly: four published entries ahead of TimesFM-3. 80% interval coverage 0.814 on average. TimesFM-3 takes 47.1 ms a series on CPU. Weights are non-commercial. The authors list covariate and multivariate use as untested in the main design.
